title: How Markets Shape Values and Political Preferences: A Field Experiment

reviewed_pages.boundary_basis: The supplied PDF has 20 pages; printed pagination runs continuously from 473 through 492, beginning with title/abstract and ending with references. No embedded supplement or appendix pages occur.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–20 (printed 473–492), including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Appendix pointers, verification materials, SI, and external sources were excluded as evidence.

experiments.name: Six-week multi-arm financial-market engagement field experiment (including 12-month follow-up)
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary causal study. All seven arms/subarms were assigned in one participant-level block randomization; the one-year follow-up reused the original assignment and therefore belongs to this experiment.

design_map.label: Exact treatment and comparator
design_map.value: Control: surveys only. Asset arms: six weekly allocations of £50 among three assets, no cash, with 10% weekly portfolio penalty for missed decisions; real stocks, sports-indexed assets, or non-incentivized fantasy stocks. Exact firms, teams, and all platform materials NR in main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables, figures, table/figure notes, footnotes, and prose were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 2 and its note earned credit for treatment/control coding and subgroup labeling; Table 1 and Table 3 were reviewed but were not treated as evidence for the separate list-experiment sample or inference. direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; compares the two eligible experiments. Cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.finding: The Swedish and U.S. co-primary experiments have the same reporting architecture and therefore the same criterion scores. Country-specific field dates, sample sources, n values, and selected numerical results differ, but neither experiment reports representation allocation probabilities, sequence generation, a fully reconstructable estimator, weighting status, error-bar construction, missingness rules, or complete numerical effects with uncertainty.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, figures, figure labels, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figures 2–7 earned credit for displayed sample sizes and group quantities. They did not earn inference credit because no note or prose defines the vertical bars. Appendix/SI pointers were treated only as evidence that information is outside the permitted source, never as evidence that omitted details were reported.

checks.treatment: Credited printed country n values and visible response distributions exactly as prose evidence would be credited.
Credited arm-specific plotted means and printed focal n values; did not infer the meaning or construction of unlabeled uncertainty bars.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. direct_comparison.scope_note: This independent session covers one paper; cross-paper synthesis is reserved for the later synthesis stage. The table compares its experiments without averaging experiment classes.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text figures and figure notes were treated as evidence on the same footing as prose. No regression table appears in the main article. Figure-note contrasts and p-values received credit where they supplied a quantity, but pointers such as ‘Coefficients are in SI’ did not supply omitted models, samples, SEs, or CIs.

checks.finding: Used plotted group quantities/error bars and the note, while recording that the error-bar construction and tests are undefined.
Used exact note-level contrasts and two-tailed p-values; did not treat SI coefficient pointers as main-article evidence.
Used exact contrasts and p-values in notes; absence of focal SEs/CIs, per-analysis N, and models remained scored missing.
Used exclusions, transformation, attrition, robustness, and threat information exactly as prose evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: 39 barangays were assigned within 13 municipalities to a town-hall deliberative campaign or business-as-usual campaigning. Official-election outcomes and the two-week post-election survey are analyses/follow-up measurements of the same original assignment, not separate experiments.

evidence.paraphrase: The survey recruited 1,314 voting-age citizens through random-walk/quota sampling.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, main-text tables, figures, and their notes received identical evidentiary status. Table 1 earned evidence for outcome columns, estimates, control quantities, fixed effects, observations, and permutation p-values; Figures 3–5 earned evidence for displayed effects, 95% intervals, LPMs, fixed effects, and clustering. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose. Conversely, SI pointers on PDF pages 5, 7–11, 13, and 16 were not treated as supplying omitted information.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 6 supplied wave interview counts and field information; footnotes 15–19 supplied estimand labels, attribute levels, and the z-test formula; figure notes supplied significance-shading rules. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared outside prose. Conversely, appendix pointers and citations did not fill main-article omissions.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; this independent session contains one paper, so cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: All three conjoint experiments report attributes, task counts, focal AMCE plots, two-way clustering, and k-sensitivity. The network-census candidate study is a supporting replication on a separate sample. Statistical transparency is essentially the same across experiments: exact randomization mechanics, outcome coding, full model specification, analyzed N, missingness rules, and interval construction are absent. The neighbor experiment additionally reports a lower-power warning but no exact focal contrast.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

Study 2 is clearer about recruitment exclusions, attrition, repeated tasks, and respondent clustering, but its conjoint ACIE computation, fitted analysis unit, assignment probabilities/restrictions, model-specific observation counts, and interval construction are not reconstructable from the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal evidence. Table 3 earned credit for OLS, outcome, controls, comparison condition, Ns, estimates, and standard errors; Figure 2 earned credit for visible contrasts, reference levels, plotted effects, and uncertainty bars. Credit was withheld only where those displays and notes jointly remained incomplete (for example SE type in Study 1 and confidence level/construction in Study 2). Appendix pointers were not treated as evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

reviewed_pages.boundary_finding: The PDF contains the complete 18-page published main article. PDF page 1 begins the title/abstract and printed page 795; PDF page 18 ends the references and carries only a notice naming online supporting-information appendices, not their contents. All 18 PDF pages were reviewed.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–18 (printed 795–812), including main-text prose, equations, figures, tables, notes, and footnotes. Online supporting information, preregistration, verification materials, code, and cited external works were excluded as evidence.
inventory_conclusion: No distinct randomized treatment-effect experiment is reported in the published main article. Random selection of survey targets is sampling, not treatment assignment. The trust game supplies a measured covariate; the main article reports no randomized manipulation or treatment contrast for it.
scope_exclusion_note: No list-experiment measurement design is described in the published main article. A reference-list citation to a list-experiment method is not a study in this paper, and Appendix C is only named in an online-SI notice whose contents are outside scope.

criterion_definitions.wording: Population and recruitment: Target population, eligibility, recruitment, and major exclusions are fully reported.
Experimental conditions: Treatment and comparator, or all randomized attributes and levels, are reported precisely enough to reproduce.
Randomization: Unit, probabilities or ratio, sequence-generation process, and restrictions are fully reported.
Outcome measurement: Outcomes, coding, timing, and primary or secondary status are fully reported.
Participant flow: Numbers recruited, randomized, exposed, followed, and analyzed are reported as applicable.
Estimand: The causal or descriptive quantity being estimated is explicitly defined.
Estimator/model: The statistical operation used to estimate the estimand is reconstructable from the text, table, or table notes.
Analysis unit: The reader can determine whether observations are participants, profiles, choices, sessions, or another unit.
Coding and reference categories: Treatment coding, outcome coding, omitted categories, and reference levels are explicit.
Specification: Covariates, fixed effects, weights, transformations, and column-to-column specification changes are explicit.
Dependence and inference: Standard errors, clustering, repeated-observation dependence, bootstrap or permutation procedures, and confidence-interval construction are explicit.
Missingness and attrition: Inclusion rules, missing outcomes, exclusions, attrition, and corresponding adjustments are explicit.
Multiplicity and analysis status: Multiple-testing procedures and prespecified versus exploratory analyses are distinguished.
Analysis sample: The number of observations used in each focal analysis is reported.
Group quantities: Relevant control means, treatment means, marginal means, or other raw quantities are reported.
Effect and uncertainty: Effect estimates and standard errors or confidence intervals are reported.
Model-to-result traceability: Each focal numerical result can be connected directly to a particular outcome, contrast, specification, sample, and inference procedure.
Robustness analyses: Alternative specifications and sensitivity analyses are explained sufficiently to understand what changed.
Internal-validity threats: Attrition, noncompliance, spillovers, demand effects, measurement problems, and other relevant threats are discussed.
Inferential scope: The paper distinguishes the randomized contrast from broader claims about mechanisms, populations, and settings.

additional_checklist.status: Omitted as instructed because no additional checklist was supplied.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.

rows.statistical_transparency_finding: No randomized experiment can be reconstructed because none is reported. The observational tables identify many model features, but the trust-game construction and survey recruitment details are delegated to excluded SI.

findings: Main-text tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, equations, prose, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status.
Table notes supplied analysis units, observation counts, clustering, fixed effects, and control information for the observational inventory map; these were credited exactly as prose would have been.
No score was reduced merely because information appeared in a display rather than prose.
Pointers to SI Sections B/D and SI Tables/Figures were recorded as pointers only and were not treated as supplying omitted details.
Random sampling of survey respondents or quiz targets was not conflated with randomized treatment assignment.

direct_comparison.summary: The two supporting experiments have the same criterion profile. Table 5 makes their OLS results unusually traceable at the result level, but neither experiment is fully reconstructable because randomization probabilities/sequence, exact treatment wording, full specification, dependence procedure, and missing-case flow are omitted. The 2018 study is somewhat clearer about setting scope because it explicitly discusses counterfactual signals and debriefing; this does not change its binary Criterion 20 score because population scope remains unbounded.

consistency_audit.standard: The same evidentiary rule was applied to prose, tables, figure notes, and table notes. Tables received full credit where they resolved an item; labels such as “s.e.” or “regress” did not substitute for an unspecified implementation.
findings: Table 1 and the full vignette jointly earned condition-reporting credit.
Tables 2–5 earned effect, uncertainty, analysis-unit, sample-size, and specification-change credit where explicit.
The tables did not earn estimator or inference-procedure credit because neither the model family nor the standard-error/CI computation is identified.
Pointers to supporting information on PDF pp. 3–5 and 13 were recorded only as pointers and supplied no omitted evidence.

experiments.name: Study 1, Experiment 1: Evidence Interpretation

evidence.paraphrase: Dates and online-survey duration are stated.

design_map.label: Experimental arms or randomized attributes
design_map.value: One of five issues (gun control, immigration, abortion, minimum wage, affirmative action) × evidence direction (liberal- vs conservative-leaning)

evidence.anchor: randomly assigned to receive information about one of five
evidence.paraphrase: Five issue levels and two directional variants are named.

design_map.label: Unit of randomization
design_map.value: Individual participant

evidence.anchor: participants were randomly assigned
evidence.paraphrase: Assignments are made to participants/respondents.

design_map.label: Allocation probabilities and restrictions
design_map.value: Evidence direction: half to each direction; issue-assignment probabilities NR. Experiment 2 issue restricted to one of four issues not received in Experiment 1; direction independent of Experiment 1.

evidence.anchor: half of participants were randomly assigned
evidence.paraphrase: Evidence direction is explicitly 1:1 for Experiment 1.

evidence.anchor: one of the four issues they did not receive
evidence.paraphrase: Experiment 2 excludes the participant's Experiment 1 issue and direction is independent.

design_map.label: Exact treatment and comparator
design_map.value: A 2×2 frequency table whose outcome-column labels are interchanged to reverse the correct liberal/conservative conclusion. Exact gun-control version shown in Figure 1; exact wording for four issues is only in excluded SI and therefore NR in full.

evidence.anchor: interchange the names of the columns
evidence.paraphrase: The manipulation reverses column labels while holding cell counts fixed.

design_map.label: Outcome definitions and timing
design_map.value: Immediate binary choice between two interpretations; 1=correct, 0=incorrect. Administered after vignette/table; primary/secondary status NR.

evidence.anchor: code as ‘1’ for correct answers and ‘0’ for incorrect answers
evidence.paraphrase: The binary outcome and coding are explicit.

design_map.label: Estimand
design_map.value: Within political-orientation group, expected probability difference between congenial and uncongenial evidence; focal asymmetry is right-wing minus left-wing difference-in-differences.

evidence.anchor: subtract the difference for left-wing respondents
evidence.paraphrase: The focal difference-in-differences and sign are defined.

design_map.label: Estimator or statistical model
design_map.value: Separate logistic regressions by evidence direction: correct indicator on binary orientation plus issue dummies; respondent-specific predicted probabilities averaged by observed-value method; separate models for issue position, ideology, party ID. Moderator models add congeniality×moderator interactions.

evidence.anchor: run separate logistic regression models
evidence.paraphrase: Model family, outcome, predictors and split are stated.

design_map.label: Analysis unit
design_map.value: Respondent (one interpretation choice per participant)

evidence.anchor: respondents’ choice over the two statements
evidence.paraphrase: Each respondent contributes a choice outcome.

design_map.label: Variable coding and reference categories
design_map.value: Outcome 0 incorrect/1 correct; left 0/right 1 for binary orientation; moderator congeniality 0 uncongenial/1 congenial. Issue-dummy omitted category and several exact scale recodes NR.

evidence.anchor: left-wing respondents are coded 0, right-wing respondents are coded 1
evidence.paraphrase: Orientation and outcome coding are given; issue reference is not.

design_map.label: Covariates and fixed effects
design_map.value: Issue-assignment dummy variables in asymmetry models; three alternative pretreatment left-right indicators; moderator models also include congeniality interactions with identity centrality and expertise. No fixed effects described.

evidence.anchor: dummy variables for issue assignment
evidence.paraphrase: The focal models include issue dummies and vary the orientation operationalization.

design_map.label: Standard-error and inference procedure
design_map.value: 95% CIs; predicted-quantity uncertainty simulated from each model's sampling distribution using observed-value averaging. Base coefficient SE/covariance estimator, simulation draws, and exact CI quantiles NR.

evidence.anchor: Uncertainty in these estimates was calculated by simulation
evidence.paraphrase: Footnote 10 gives the broad predictive simulation and observed-value averaging approach.

design_map.label: Handling of clustering or repeated observations
design_map.value: No clustering reported; each scored task yields one outcome (Experiment 1) or two outcomes (Experiment 2) per respondent, analyzed separately. Cross-task dependence is not discussed.

evidence.anchor: separate logistic regression models
evidence.paraphrase: The main text describes separate outcome models but no dependence adjustment.

design_map.label: Missing-data and attrition rules
design_map.value: Two attention checks exclude 13%; moderates and independents excluded from binary left-right analyses; missing survey-item/outcome handling and adjustment NR.

evidence.anchor: Independents and moderates are excluded
evidence.paraphrase: The binary orientation analyses exclude those groups.

design_map.label: Effect estimates and uncertainty
design_map.value: Figure 2 plots predicted probabilities and 95% CIs plus asymmetry differences; text summarizes congeniality changes as 10–20 percentage points. Exact numeric point estimates/CI endpoints NR.

evidence.anchor: between 10 and 20 percentage points
evidence.paraphrase: Text provides a range and Figure 2 displays point/interval estimates.

design_map.value: Age 18+ and U.S. adult; no other eligibility reported

evidence.anchor: U.S adults aged 18 years and older

evidence.anchor: Our sample was drawn from Lucid
evidence.paraphrase: Lucid supplied an online nonprobability pool and demographic/region quotas.

design_map.label: Field dates and setting

evidence.anchor: participate in a 15-minute survey between May 22-24, 2018
evidence.paraphrase: Dates and online-survey duration are stated.

design_map.label: Number recruited and analyzed
design_map.value: 2,085 recruited; 1,816 final analytical sample after 87% passed two attention checks

evidence.anchor: final analytical sample of 1,816 respondents
evidence.paraphrase: The article reports recruited and final counts plus the attention-check pass fraction.

design_map.label: Experimental arms or randomized attributes
design_map.value: One of the four issues not assigned in Experiment 1 × independent evidence direction (liberal- vs conservative-supporting conclusion)

evidence.anchor: one of the four issues they did not receive
evidence.paraphrase: Issue is randomized subject to a prior-issue exclusion; direction is independently randomized.

design_map.label: Unit of randomization
design_map.value: Individual participant

evidence.anchor: participants were randomly assigned
evidence.paraphrase: Assignments are made to participants/respondents.

design_map.label: Allocation probabilities and restrictions
design_map.value: Evidence direction: half to each direction; issue-assignment probabilities NR. Experiment 2 issue restricted to one of four issues not received in Experiment 1; direction independent of Experiment 1.

evidence.anchor: half of participants were randomly assigned
evidence.paraphrase: Evidence direction is explicitly 1:1 for Experiment 1.

evidence.anchor: one of the four issues they did not receive
evidence.paraphrase: Experiment 2 excludes the participant's Experiment 1 issue and direction is independent.

design_map.label: Exact treatment and comparator
design_map.value: Short study summary with finding direction reversed by interchanging increase/decrease. Exact minimum-wage version shown; exact wording for other issues is only in excluded SI and therefore NR in full.

evidence.anchor: interchanging the words ‘increase’ and ‘decrease’
evidence.paraphrase: The minimum-wage directional manipulation is fully exemplified, but other vignettes are omitted.

design_map.label: Outcome definitions and timing
design_map.value: Immediately after vignette: sample-size adequacy on 7 points from much smaller to much larger than necessary; causal-evidence agreement on 7 points from disagree strongly to agree strongly. Both standardized to mean 0, SD 1; primary/secondary status NR.

evidence.anchor: Participants responded on a 7-point scale
evidence.paraphrase: Both response scales and subsequent standardization are described.

design_map.label: Estimand
design_map.value: Within political-orientation group, expected standardized-outcome difference between congenial and uncongenial findings; focal asymmetry is right-wing minus left-wing difference-in-differences.

evidence.anchor: difference between conditions in expected values
evidence.paraphrase: The PMR contrast and higher-level difference-in-differences are explicit.

design_map.label: Estimator or statistical model
design_map.value: Separate OLS models for standardized sample-size and causality outcomes using orientation and issue dummies within evidence-direction strata; observed-value predicted outcomes; three orientation operationalizations. Moderator models add congeniality interactions.

evidence.anchor: estimate linear models using ordinary least squares
evidence.paraphrase: Outcome models, transformations and prediction step are stated.

design_map.label: Analysis unit
design_map.value: Respondent; two outcomes modeled separately

evidence.anchor: Participants were then asked to evaluate
evidence.paraphrase: Each participant supplies both ratings, which are analyzed as separate outcomes.

design_map.label: Variable coding and reference categories
design_map.value: Outcomes standardized; orientation left 0/right 1; moderator congeniality 0 uncongenial/1 congenial. Exact numeric coding direction of the original 7-point scales is inferable from anchors but not stated as numbers; issue omitted category NR.

evidence.anchor: standardized, such that they have a mean of zero
evidence.paraphrase: Transformations and orientation coding are stated, but model reference details are incomplete.

design_map.label: Covariates and fixed effects
design_map.value: Issue-assignment dummy variables in asymmetry models; three alternative pretreatment left-right indicators; moderator models also include congeniality interactions with identity centrality and expertise. No fixed effects described.

evidence.anchor: dummy variables for issue assignment
evidence.paraphrase: The focal models include issue dummies and vary the orientation operationalization.

design_map.label: Standard-error and inference procedure
design_map.value: 95% CIs; predicted-quantity uncertainty simulated from each model's sampling distribution using observed-value averaging. Base coefficient SE/covariance estimator, simulation draws, and exact CI quantiles NR.

evidence.anchor: Uncertainty in these estimates was calculated by simulation
evidence.paraphrase: Footnote 10 gives the broad predictive simulation and observed-value averaging approach.

design_map.label: Handling of clustering or repeated observations
design_map.value: No clustering reported; each scored task yields one outcome (Experiment 1) or two outcomes (Experiment 2) per respondent, analyzed separately. Cross-task dependence is not discussed.

evidence.anchor: separate logistic regression models
evidence.paraphrase: The main text describes separate outcome models but no dependence adjustment.

design_map.label: Missing-data and attrition rules
design_map.value: Two attention checks exclude 13%; moderates and independents excluded from binary left-right analyses; missing survey-item/outcome handling and adjustment NR.

evidence.anchor: Independents and moderates are excluded
evidence.paraphrase: The binary orientation analyses exclude those groups.

design_map.label: Effect estimates and uncertainty
design_map.value: Figure 2 plots predicted standardized outcomes and 95% CIs plus asymmetry differences; text summarizes bias as 0.15–0.30 SD. Exact numeric point estimates/CI endpoints NR.

evidence.anchor: between 0.15 and 0.30 standard deviations
evidence.paraphrase: Text supplies a range and Figure 2 supplies point/interval displays.

rows.summary: Strong visible result reporting, but randomization, complete specification, missingness, and scope details are insufficient for full reconstruction.
Only pooled attention/recall percentages are reported; sample, arm contrasts, model, and inference are absent.

findings: Tables, figure notes, table notes, footnotes, and prose were treated as equal main-article evidence.
Figure 4/5 arm means, Ns, confidence intervals, and contrast p-values received full evidentiary credit where they directly supplied a required element.

Table 2 and its note received full credit for the linear estimator, coefficient/SE reporting, column samples, and iteration-level clustering; missing or inconsistent adjustment details were not inferred.
Pointers to the SI Appendix, preanalysis plan, and verification archive were recorded but never used to fill omitted information.
Absence judgments were checked across PDF pages 1–16 and the relevant displays; no invented quotation was used for an absence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.finding: Studies 2 and 3 are substantially more transparent than the diagnostic Studies 4 and 5 because they print models, dependence structure, and numerical uncertainty. Even Studies 2 and 3 are not fully reconstructable: allocation/sequence details, full stimulus wording, outcome/reference coding, inference construction, missing-data rules, per-analysis observation counts, raw condition quantities, and complete attrition-threat discussion are incomplete. Study 2 meets 7/20 core items and Study 3 meets 6/20; Study 4 meets 1/20 and Study 5 meets 2/20.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 4's note earned evidence for model family, random/fixed effects, and 95% intervals. Figure examples did not earn credit for omitted complete stimulus sets. Pointers to supporting information or replication materials did not supply missing information.
checks: Figure 4 note credited for linear mixed-effects models, participant random effects, vignette fixed effects, and 95% CI error bars.
Footnotes 10, 11, and 14 credited for analysis status and exclusions.
Figure 3 and Figure 5 credited as examples only, not as complete treatment documentation.
Supporting-information pointers on printed pages 783, 785, 787, and 790 were not treated as evidence of the omitted content.

experiments.name: 1990–1992 and 1992–1994–1996 NES panel analyses
experiments.classification_rationale: Observational analysis: no new randomized assignment; cross-lagged OLS models relate measured welfare feelings and racial predispositions over time.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied; separate checklist scoring is omitted.

direct_comparison.finding: All three experiments precisely report vignette content and focal slope differences, but none reports complete randomization procedures, model-specific Ns, variance-estimator details, or full focal model specifications in the main article. The 1991 experiment is relatively more transparent because it names base covariates and describes placebo/robustness checks; the 2014 and 2015 models rely more heavily on excluded SI pointers.

findings: Main-text prose, figure notes, footnotes, and Table 1 notes were given equal evidentiary status.
Figure-note interaction t statistics earned uncertainty credit just as prose p values did.
No credit was withheld merely because evidence appeared in a display or note.
Conversely, Figures 1–3 do not contain model Ns, complete specifications, standard-error methods, or raw arm means; pointers to SI tables were not treated as supplying those facts.
Table 1 was inspected visually and used only to classify the NES panel work as observational; it was not scored as an experiment.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 2 supplied exact pooled ITT estimates and p-values for Studies 1–2; Figures 1, 4, and 7 and their notes supplied labeled contrasts and uncertainty. No score was reduced merely because evidence was in a display. Appendix pointers were recorded only as pointers and never treated as evidence of omitted content.

experiments.classification_rationale: The article expressly calls these observational analyses; victimization and perceived volition are measured, not randomized.

findings: Table 1 supplied the conjoint attribute levels and female-only marriage restriction and received full evidentiary weight.
Table 2 supplied act-specific raw punishment distributions; it did not substitute for missing raw identity-attribute quantities.
Figure 1 and Figure 2 labels/notes supplied reference categories, 95% intervals, and respondent-clustered robust standard errors with the same status as prose.
Figure 3 and Table 3 were treated as evidence for the explicitly observational volition analysis, not as a new randomized experiment.
Footnotes 19, 21, 24, and 25 were credited for what they state; pointers to SI were not treated as reporting omitted methods or results.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Include primary and embedded list experiments. Apply the list-experiment instructions and experiment classification rules in the shared research prompt.

title: International Status Concerns and Domestic Support for Political Leaders

reviewed_pages.boundary_note: All 16 PDF pages are the published main article. PDF page 16 ends with a Supporting Information availability list; no appendix content is embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–16 (printed 732–747), including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Appendix pointers, verification materials, and all external sources were excluded.

additional_checklist.note: No additional reporting checklist was supplied.

inventory_notes: Seven scored randomized experiments were identified: four primary 2016 SSI scenario experiments, two supporting 2018 MTurk replications, and one supporting 2019 MTurk ENE.
Post-treatment question-order randomization is a procedural feature of the scenario experiments, not a separate sampled experiment.
Randomized presidential affiliation is an embedded attribute of the ENE; no separate outcome analysis is reported.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1, its note, figure/table notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned credit for OLS identification, per-column sample sizes, coefficients, standard errors, dependent-variable range/direction, and field fixed effects. It did not earn credit for details the table and note omit, including allocation, treatment pooling, reference categories, SE computation, clustering, and missing-data rules. Appendix pointers supplied no omitted information.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment comparison; only one paper is in this independent session.
direct_comparison.summary: Experiment 1 is more statistically transparent because Equations 1–4 identify its ordered Bradley–Terry hierarchy, coding, analysis unit, and a main-text controlled robustness model. Experiment 2 clearly defines the policy-specific difference in means but omits the right-panel association model, arm-by-issue sample sizes, outcome recode, dependence adjustment, and interval construction. Neither experiment is fully reconstructable from the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figure content, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Credit was awarded from Figure 1/4 prompt wording, Equations 1–5, Figure 2/3/5 notes, and footnotes where they supplied components. Appendix pointers and the Supporting Information list were treated only as evidence that information is outside the main article, never as evidence that the omitted information was reported.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal main-article evidence. Table 1 earned credit for labeled arms, providers, and sample sizes; figure notes earned credit for OLS, standardization, broad contrasts, plotted estimates, and confidence intervals. They did not earn credit for omitted details such as exact stimulus/outcome wording, allocation probabilities, complete coding, model specifications, per-model Ns, standard-error procedures, or CI construction. Appendix pointers were treated only as evidence that information was outside scope.

records.example: Table 1 supports treatment labels and experiment-level sample sizes.
Figures 1–5 support plotted effects/CIs, OLS descriptions, standardization, and stated baselines.
Pointers to instrumentation, recruitment details, regression tables, and robustness checks did not fill main-article omissions.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is deferred because this session contains one paper.
direct_comparison.finding: The three primary experiments have the same criterion-level transparency profile: estimands and respondent analysis units are identifiable and effects/CIs are plotted, but exact stimuli/outcomes, allocation, complete coding/specification, inference details, per-model samples, missingness, multiplicity, and population scope are not reconstructable from the main article.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper session; comparison is between the two scored experiments, not across papers.
direct_comparison.summary: Both experiments fully report vignette conditions and graphical group quantities/effects. Study 1 adds a preregistration statement and a 2×2 reputation manipulation; Study 2 reports partial exclusion rules and a four-arm replication/extension. Neither reports allocation probabilities/sequence generation, per-analysis Ns, full coding/specifications, or bootstrap/CI construction, so their core subtotal profiles are identical.

findings: Tables 1 and 2 received full evidentiary status for exact treatment and comparator text.
Figures 2–7 and their notes received full evidentiary status for plotted means, effect estimates, model labels, confidence intervals, and broad analysis descriptions.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
Display notes did not receive extra credit when they named OLS, bootstrap, or mediation without enough implementation detail to reconstruct the analysis.
Pointers to appendices, preregistration, and verification materials were treated only as pointers; omitted content was not credited.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: Campaign Messages, Polling, and Elections: Theory and Experimental Evidence

reviewed_pages.boundary_note: All 19 PDF pages are the published main article. PDF page 19 ends with a pointer to online Supporting Information; no supporting appendix is embedded or used.

source_scope: Published main article only: main text, tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. Online SI, verification materials, instructions, external references, and all other research files were excluded.

additional_checklist.note: No additional checklist was supplied.

inventory_note: One distinct randomized experiment identified. No category 2–5 studies and no list-experiment measurement designs were identified. The postexperiment lottery task is a covariate measurement, not a reported randomized experiment; the universal straw poll is not randomized.

experiments.name: Repeated-election laboratory experiment (messages × quality variance)
experiments.classification_rationale: The article's sole randomized study is the primary 2×2 laboratory experiment used to test H1–H6. Repeated random grouping, challenger nomination, and quality draws are constituent randomizations within the same subjects and supergames, not new randomized samples or manipulations.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.statistical_transparency: The treatment texts, arm counts, outcome questions, timing, adjusted arm predictions, and focal p-values are visible in the main article. Reconstruction fails chiefly because assignment generation/probabilities, exact model/covariates, analysis Ns, missing-data rules, and inference/error-bar construction are not reported.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1 and its note, Figure 6 and its note, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned full treatment-text evidence; Figure 6 earned group-quantity evidence but not estimator/inference credit because its note does not identify the model, covariate set, error bars, or CI construction. Appendix pointers supplied no evidence.
findings: Table 1 and its note establish exact prime wording, the no-prime comparator, mutually exclusive exposure, and realized arm counts.
Figure 6 and its note establish adjusted arm predictions and that covariates were held at means; they do not establish which covariates, the model/link, or the meaning of error bars.
The democracy result is p=.049 in prose for the original scale but p=.064 in Figure 6 after dichotomization (footnote 8); both were retained without treating them as the same specification.
For violence, prose on printed p. 522 reports p=.005 while Figure 6 reports p=.009; this display/text discrepancy is flagged for human review.
References to the online appendix, preregistration, and results available from authors were not credited.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; comparison is between its two scored experiments, not a cross-paper synthesis.
direct_comparison.findings: Wave 2 and wave 3 have the same criterion profile (6/20): both clearly report the focal estimand, estimator family, participant analysis unit, focal sample sizes, effects/95% intervals, and inferential scope. Neither fully reports exact stimuli, randomization implementation, factor scoring, variance/CI construction, missingness, multiplicity, or reproducible robustness checks. Wave 3 more directly discusses the outcome-wording measurement problem, but this does not change criterion 19 because other validity threats remain unaddressed.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Figure notes earned credit for models, sample sizes, contrasts, and 95% intervals; Table 2 earned credit for item wording; Tables 3–4 earned credit for loadings/reliability. Appendix pointers earned no credit for omitted content.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, figure notes, tables, table notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status when they were inside the published main article. Figure 7/8 labels and notes earned credit for levels, references, effect estimates, and 95% CIs. Table 4 and its note were used for inventory/context but did not convert the RDD into a randomized experiment. Pointers to Supporting Information were recorded only as evidence that details are absent from the permitted source, never as substantive evidence.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

title: Can Online Civic Education Induce Democratic Citizenship? Experimental Evidence from a New Democracy

reviewed_page_details.boundary_note: All 18 PDF pages were reviewed. PDF p. 18 contains the end of the references and a Supporting Information notice that only lists online appendices; no appendix content is embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text prose, figures, tables, notes, and footnotes. Online appendices A–G, preregistration, registry, Dataverse, replication files, and external references were excluded as evidence.
scope_exclusions_summary: No list-experiment measurement design was identified in the main article. The phrase ‘listing survey’ denotes the baseline survey, not a list experiment.

experiments.name: Four-arm online civic-education video experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: The article's central causal study is one participant-level randomization into three substantive treatment arms and one shared placebo, followed immediately by formal OLS and Wald analyses. experiments.name: Session-level institutional-quality laboratory experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary causal experiment. A single sample was assigned at session level to three institutional-quality conditions, completed a public-good exposure phase, and then supplied trust-game outcomes under the original assignment. Role/order randomizations are implementation steps within this experiment, not separate experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: single-paper independent assessment
direct_comparison.summary: Cross-paper comparison is not possible in this one-paper session. Within AJPS059, tables and Equation 2 make outcomes, contrasts, covariates, fixed effects, clustered SEs, Ns, estimates and column mappings unusually traceable. Exact random-sequence/probability details, inverse-probability weights, RI implementation, participant flow, attrition, multiplicity, and most raw group quantities remain unreconstructable from the main article.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper session; cross-paper comparison is not possible here. The table compares the two eligible experimental blocks without combining them.
direct_comparison.finding: The party-affiliated block is more transparent because Table 1 identifies its linear model, profile-level samples, coefficients, standard errors, covariates, fixed effects, and respondent clustering. The no-party block is presented only through marginal-mean figures lacking N and computational/inference details. Neither block fully reports allocation probabilities, sequence generation, participant flow, missing-data rules, multiplicity, exact marginal-mean construction, or all internal-validity threats.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, table bodies, table notes, figure bodies, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status when they appeared in the published main article. Table 1 and its note earned credit for model, unit, sample size, estimates, uncertainty, covariates/fixed effects, and clustering without requiring a redundant equation. Figures 2–3 earned credit for displayed marginal means and uncertainty bars, but not for unreported N or interval construction. Appendix pointers earned no substantive credit.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given the same evidentiary status. Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–5 received affirmative credit where they supplied conditions, coding, sample sizes, estimates, uncertainty, and contrast mapping. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose. Appendix pointers on PDF page 18 and in main-text notes were not treated as supplied evidence.

checks.finding: Credited for treatment levels and the fixed deaths/cases restriction; not credited for allocation probabilities or full assignment mechanics.
Credited for outcome equations, open-border reference, estimates, standard errors, and analysis Ns; not credited for an unstated standard-error calculation.
Credited for displayed estimands, contrasts, estimates, 95% intervals, and named bootstrap types; not credited for omitted bootstrap/CI implementation details.
Credited for the reported outcome-ordinality concern and model choice.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison of the two distinct randomized samples; no cross-paper synthesis is attempted in this one-paper session.
direct_comparison.finding: The UK and US experiments have identical reporting structures and therefore identical criterion scores. Country-specific tables separately report N, coefficients, and standard errors; shared methods and combined figures identify country panels and contrasts. Neither experiment reports allocation probabilities, assignment sequence generation, participant flow beyond recruited/analyzed totals, complete weight/covariate coding, missingness rules, multiplicity status, or full inference implementation.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, table content, table notes, figure content, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 earned condition-level credit; Figures 2–7 and their notes earned results credit where complete. The same displays did not earn model credit when they omitted coding, specifications, sample sizes, or inference procedures. Pointers to supporting information were recorded only as evidence that details are absent from the main article.
checks: Table 1 was used as positive evidence for exact randomized attributes and levels.
Figure 3 and its note were used as positive evidence for marginal quantities and its pair-dropping rule.
Figure 7 header was used as positive evidence for nested-stage profile counts.
Footnotes 16, 20, and 21 were treated like prose: their reported facts counted, while SI pointers did not import excluded information.

findings: Figure 1 and its note received full evidentiary status for arm definitions, arm counts, outcomes, and flow.
Figures 3–7 and their notes received full evidentiary status for contrasts, analysis Ns, point estimates, and 95% confidence intervals.
Footnotes received the same evidentiary status as prose, including flow (footnote 9), index construction (footnote 14), and the demand/order threat (footnote 21).
Pointers to Tables/Figures A1–A9 and the preregistration were recorded only as pointers; excluded materials did not cure main-article omissions.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a figure or note rather than prose.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; no cross-paper ranking is possible in this session.

rows.summary: Conditions and graphical results are clearer than the statistical implementation: estimator, assignment probabilities, SE/CI construction, and missing-data rules are not reconstructable.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.

consistency_audit.standard: The same binary full-reporting rule was applied to prose, tables, figures, notes, and footnotes. A display earned credit when it supplied the required information; graphical reporting was accepted for effects and uncertainty. Appendix pointers did not supply omitted content.
findings: Figures 2–5 received credit for reporting effect estimates and 90% confidence intervals because their axes, rows, panels, and notes visibly map outcomes and contrasts.
Tables 2–3 received credit for the quantities they actually report (model labels, standard errors, and Ns), but their subgroup/household Ns were not imputed to focal Figures 2–5.
The names OLS, 2SLS/CACE, randomization inference, BART, and Benjamini–Hochberg were not treated as sufficient where implementation details remained absent.

Statements sending question wording, randomization-inference results, multiplicity results, mediation, heterogeneity, and attrition details to online appendices were treated as absences under the source restriction.
No information was credited based on customary practice, the verification-material notice, preregistration availability, or cited methods articles.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. experiments.name: Three-arm WhatsApp civic-education course experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment. findings: Tables, figure notes, table notes, footnotes, and prose were treated as equal main-article evidence.
Figure 1 supplied flow and realized arm counts; Tables 1–6 supplied outcomes, controls, reference groups, sample sizes, estimates, and group means wherever explicit.
No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
Unlabeled parenthetical values were not assumed to be standard errors, and appendix pointers were not treated as evidence.

experiments.name: Six-case belief-correction survey experiment

Later diagnostic and robustness outcomes use this original assignment.

Manipulation checks, placebo-site outcomes, subgroup analyses, and RI reuse this assignment and are part of the same experiment.

design_map.label: Target population
design_map.value: Vietnamese respondents represented by the nationwide PAPI citizen survey, with deliberate inclusion of internal migrants and permanent residents.

evidence.anchor: Our final sample yields a total of 812 migrants and 15,021 permanent residents
evidence.paraphrase: The sampling account gives a final total of 15,833 respondents, split into 812 migrants and 15,021 permanent residents.

design_map.label: Recruitment procedure
design_map.value: Multistage PAPI sample: districts, communes and villages selected using PPS with locality capitals as certainty units; 20 individuals per village by simple random sampling; upgraded lists sampled nonpermanent residents in 12 receiving provinces.

evidence.anchor: Within each village, 20 individuals are selected ... using simple random sampling
evidence.paraphrase: PAPI used multistage PPS sampling through districts, communes and villages; 20 people per village were selected by simple random sampling, with added migrant lists in receiving provinces.

rows.statistical_transparency: The randomized attributes, OLS label, respondent clustering, and plotted effects/CIs are clear. Reconstruction fails chiefly on the exact conjoint estimand, regression analysis unit, exact coding/model specification, figure-specific sample sizes, CI construction, and missingness/multiplicity rules.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figure notes, table notes, and footnotes were treated as coequal main-article evidence. Table 1 earned experimental-condition credit; figure notes earned estimator, clustering, and uncertainty credit. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display, and no appendix pointer supplied omitted evidence.

checks.result: Table 1 and its note were used to score attributes/levels exactly as prose would be.
Figures 2–8 and notes supplied OLS, respondent clustering, outcome/contrast labels, estimates, and 95% interval evidence.
Unreported equal probabilities, outcome coding, covariate absence, profile-row construction, and CI formula were not inferred.
References to Supporting Information Figures/Appendices and verification files were recorded only as pointers, never as evidence of their contents.

execution_record.assessment_scope: Exclude list-experiment measurement designs from scoring. For papers with substantive treatment-effect experiments and embedded list measurements, assess the substantive experiments. Record the list measurement designs separately in a top-level scope_exclusions array with name, reason and source pages, and summarize these exclusions in the HTML. This scope restriction takes precedence over the shared prompt's list-experiment scoring section; retain the shared criteria for eligible experiments.
